question_text: A helicopter lands $5\text{ km}$ east and $7\text{ km}$ south of its starting point.

subparts.stem: Find the helicopter's distance from its starting point.

mark_breakdown.desc: Find median and quartiles from the 19 ordered values

subparts.solution:
The ordered data set is:
$4, 9, 10, 12, 12, 14, 14, 15, 16, 16, 16, 17, 18, 18, 18, 20, 23, 26, 31$ ($19$ data values)
$$\text{median} = 16 \quad (\text{10th value})$$
Lower half ($9$ values): $4, 9, 10, 12, 12, 14, 14, 15, 16 \implies Q_1 = 12$
Upper half ($9$ values): $16, 17, 18, 18, 18, 20, 23, 26, 31 \implies Q_3 = 18$
So the five-number summary is:
$$\begin{cases} \text{minimum} = 4 \\ Q_1 = 12 \\ \text{median} = 16 \\ Q_3 = 18 \\ \text{maximum} = 31 \end{cases}$$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The five-number summary consists of the minimum, first quartile ($Q_1$), median, third quartile ($Q_3$), and maximum.
step_by_step: There are 19 values. The median is the 10th value, which is 16.
Excluding the 10th value gives 9 values below it; the median of these 9 values is the 5th value: $Q_1 = 12$.
Excluding the 10th value gives 9 values above it; the median of these 9 values is the 15th value overall (5th of the upper half): $Q_3 = 18$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Including the median when finding the quartiles of an odd-sized dataset.
